info.name: ClinicalHarmony · Phase 9c — Gold over Kafka
info.description: Happy-path walkthrough (8 requests) of Phase 9c: clinicalharmony.silver.patient.changed → gold-builder (inside fhir-compliance-service) → US Core FHIR + validator → Gold via GoldWriter, lineage BRONZE → SILVER → GOLD → outbox → clinicalharmony.gold.patient.changed → pmi-matcher (inside patient-index-service) → one debounced matching run. MLLP isn't HTTP, so messages are sent by the generator from a terminal (see request 2); Postman checks the results through the api-gateway and Kafbat UI. Prereqs: `docker-compose up -d`, migration 25 applied. Failure paths (broken event → DLT, redelivery, busy PMI lock, max-delay in a steady stream) are covered by scripts/smoke-test.sh section 20 and the integration / unit tests.

item.name: 1. Auth — sign in as dana (data steward)

request.description: DEV-ONLY password grant on client clinicalharmony-dashboard-dev (same as the Phase 7 / 9b collections) so the gateway's read models can be called. Tokens live 10 minutes — re-run 1 on a 401.

item.name: 2. FHIR Viewer — US Core AllergyIntolerance built from Silver, newest first

request.description: Run the generator first, in a terminal from the repo root:  python3 data-generator/generate.py --seed 919  (100 seeded ADT / ORU / RDE messages over MLLP to :8887; it prints the cross-facility duplicates it planted, by source + MRN + DOB). Nothing else to call: silver-transformer announces each changed patient on clinicalharmony.silver.patient.changed, and fhir-compliance-service's gold-builder rebuilds that patient's US Core resources into Gold through GoldWriter — now including AllergyIntolerance from silver.allergies (HL7 AL1). Saves the newest one's Gold id.

item.name: 3. Data Lineage — that resource traced back to the raw HL7 message

request.description: The gold.data_lineage chain GoldWriter wrote: BRONZE (the raw HL7 v2 message, its SHA-256 as input hash, via MLLP → Kafka → bronze-listener-service) → SILVER (silver-transformer-service's silver.allergies row) → GOLD (the FHIR resource, with the stored JSON's hash). bronzeMessages holds the raw message itself.

item.name: 4. PMI — matching ran by itself after the Gold events

request.description: patient-index-service's pmi-matcher consumes clinicalharmony.gold.patient.changed and debounces it: ONE matching run 5 s after the last event of a burst (at most every 30 s while events keep coming), triggered_by "kafka:pmi-matcher (<n> events, <m> masters)". No POST /match/run needed.

The generator registers ~10% of patients at BOTH CITY_HOSPITAL and NORTH_CLINIC under different MRNs. The IDENTICAL ones (same name, DOB, address, ZIP, phone) match the deterministic rule EXACT_NAME_DOB_PLUS_PHONE_OR_ZIP and are merged into one master automatically. Saves that master's id.

item.name: 6. PMI Review — fuzzy cross-facility duplicates wait for a data steward

exec: pm.test('a 0.619 pair is queued', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().some(c => Number(c.score) === 0.619)).to.eql(true));

request.description: The FUZZY duplicates differ in the birth DAY (a typo: same year and month) and the phone: weighted score 13 / 21 = 0.619, inside the review band 0.60–0.85, so they're queued — accept or reject them on the dashboard's PMI Review (dana).

item.name: 7. Kafka — gold-builder consumer group (Kafbat UI API)

request.description: Lag 0 = every silver.patient.changed event has been built into Gold. Open http://localhost:8090 to browse clinicalharmony.gold.patient.changed (key = master id; value = the master, the resources written and their US Core compliance).

item.name: 8. Kafka — pmi-matcher consumer group (Kafbat UI API)

request.description: Lag 0 = every gold.patient.changed event has been seen by the PMI (runs themselves are debounced, see 4).
